RC1.label: Product or software defect

RC1.1.label: Known bug or open defect
RC1.1.description: The issue matches a known defect already logged by the engineering team.

RC1.2.label: Regression from a recent release
RC1.2.description: A previously working feature broke following a software update or deployment.

RC1.3.label: Edge case or untested scenario
RC1.3.description: The system behaves incorrectly in a specific configuration or use case that was not covered in testing.

RC1.4.label: Missing feature causing workaround failure
RC1.4.description: An absent feature forces the customer into a workaround that itself fails or is unsustainable.

RC1.5.label: Other product defect
RC1.5.description: A product or software defect that does not fit another sub-category.

RC1.description: The issue was caused by a bug, regression, or design flaw in the product or software itself. The system did not behave as designed.

RC2.label: Process or policy failure

RC2.1.label: Incorrect procedure applied
RC2.1.description: The correct process exists but was applied incorrectly in this instance.

RC2.2.label: Policy gap or ambiguity
RC2.2.description: The existing policy does not clearly cover this scenario, leading to inconsistent handling.

RC2.3.label: Process handoff breakdown
RC2.3.description: The issue occurred at the boundary between teams, systems, or process steps where a handoff was required.

RC2.4.label: Missing verification or approval step
RC2.4.description: A required verification, review, or approval was not performed as part of the process.

RC2.5.label: Other process or policy failure
RC2.5.description: A process or policy issue that does not fit another sub-category.

RC2.description: The issue was caused by an incorrect, unclear, or missing internal process or policy, rather than a product defect or individual error.

RC3.label: Agent or human error

RC3.1.label: Incorrect information provided
RC3.1.description: Agent gave the customer wrong information about the product, policy, or process.

RC3.2.label: Wrong action taken on account or system
RC3.2.description: Agent performed an incorrect action (e.g. wrong setting changed, incorrect refund amount, case closed prematurely).

RC3.3.label: Insufficient investigation before resolution
RC3.3.description: Agent resolved the issue without fully diagnosing the root cause, leading to recurrence.

RC3.4.label: Failure to follow up as committed
RC3.4.description: Agent committed to a follow-up action but did not complete it within the agreed timeframe.

RC3.5.label: Other agent error
RC3.5.description: An agent or human error that does not fit another sub-category.

RC3.description: The issue was caused or worsened by an error made by a support agent or other employee, including incorrect information, wrong actions, or omissions.

RC4.label: Customer error or misunderstanding

RC4.1.label: Incorrect product usage
RC4.1.description: Customer was not using the product or feature as designed or documented.

RC4.2.label: Misunderstood product terms or policy
RC4.2.description: Customer had a misunderstanding about what the product offers, the terms of service, or the returns or billing policy.

RC4.3.label: Incorrect expectation set at purchase
RC4.3.description: Customer's expectation of what the product would do does not match reality, possibly due to misleading marketing or sales communication.

RC4.4.label: Failed to follow provided instructions
RC4.4.description: Customer was given correct instructions but did not follow them, leading to the issue.

RC4.5.label: Other customer error
RC4.5.description: A customer error or misunderstanding that does not fit another sub-category.

RC4.description: The issue was caused by the customer using the product incorrectly, misunderstanding instructions, or having incorrect expectations.

RC5.label: Infrastructure or system failure

RC5.1.label: Service outage or downtime
RC5.1.description: The product or a dependent service was completely unavailable due to an infrastructure failure.

RC5.2.label: Performance degradation due to infrastructure
RC5.2.description: Slow response times, timeouts, or instability caused by infrastructure capacity or health issues.

RC5.3.label: Data integrity or synchronisation issue
RC5.3.description: Data was lost, duplicated, or became inconsistent across systems due to a pipeline or synchronisation failure.

RC5.4.label: Security or access control infrastructure issue
RC5.4.description: Authentication, authorisation, or security systems failed, causing access problems.

RC5.5.label: Other infrastructure failure
RC5.5.description: An infrastructure issue that does not fit another sub-category.

RC5.description: The issue was caused by an outage, degradation, or failure in the underlying infrastructure, platform, or data systems - outside of the product codebase itself.

RC6.label: Third-party dependency failure

RC6.1.label: Payment processor or financial third party
RC6.1.description: A payment gateway, bank, or financial service provider caused the issue.

RC6.2.label: Logistics or carrier partner
RC6.2.description: A shipping carrier, courier, or logistics provider caused the delivery issue.

RC6.3.label: Identity or SSO provider
RC6.3.description: An SSO provider, identity platform, or federated login system caused the authentication issue.

RC6.4.label: Cloud or infrastructure provider
RC6.4.description: A cloud platform provider (e.g. AWS, Azure, GCP) experienced an issue that affected service.

RC6.5.label: Other third-party failure
RC6.5.description: A third-party failure that does not fit another sub-category.

RC6.description: The issue originated in a third-party service, partner system, or external provider that the company depends on.

RC7.label: Configuration or setup issue

RC7.1.label: Incorrect account or product settings
RC7.1.description: Account-level or product-level settings were configured incorrectly by the customer or during onboarding.

RC7.2.label: Permission or role misconfiguration
RC7.2.description: User permissions, roles, or access controls were set up incorrectly.

RC7.3.label: Integration or connector misconfiguration
RC7.3.description: A third-party integration, webhook, or API connector was not configured correctly.

RC7.4.label: Other configuration issue
RC7.4.description: A configuration or setup issue that does not fit another sub-category.

RC7.description: The issue was caused by incorrect configuration of the product, account settings, or integration - not a product bug, but a setup error.

RC8.label: Communication or notification failure

RC8.1.label: Expected notification not sent
RC8.1.description: A system notification, confirmation email, alert, or reminder that should have been triggered was not sent.

RC8.2.label: Incorrect or misleading notification content
RC8.2.description: A notification was sent but contained incorrect information, wrong details, or misleading instructions.

RC8.3.label: Documentation gap or inaccuracy
RC8.3.description: The product documentation, help articles, or FAQs did not cover the scenario or contained incorrect information.

RC8.4.label: Other communication failure
RC8.4.description: A communication or notification failure that does not fit another sub-category.

RC8.description: The issue was caused by a failure in how information was communicated to the customer: missing notifications, incorrect communications, or unclear documentation.
